title: Rehabilitated University of Benghazi Reopens After Years of Reconstruction
detail: The University of Benghazi held an extravagant reopening ceremony on Friday, September 4, 2026, after the Fund for the Development and Reconstruction of Libya (FDRL), directed by Belgasem Haftar, completed a full rehabilitation of the campus that was destroyed during the fighting that flattened much of Benghazi. The ceremony was attended by House of Representatives Speaker Aguila Saleh, First Deputy Speaker Fawzi Al-Nuwairi, Second Deputy Speaker Misbah Douma, GNS Prime Minister Osama Hamad, and LNA Commander-in-Chief Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar. Officials described the project as upgrading higher-education infrastructure to provide an integrated university environment 'befitting the university's stature, history, and its academic and national role.' The reopening came a day before the second Libyan-American Development and Reconstruction Forum convened in Benghazi under the same FDRL reconstruction push.

title: Zawia Power Station's Third Unit Returns to National Grid After Delayed GE Vernova Maintenance
detail: The General Electricity Company of Libya (GECOL) reconnected the third unit of the Zawia Combined-Cycle Power Station to the national grid on September 4, 2026, restoring 150 MW of capacity after US firm GE Vernova completed a long-delayed overhaul. The maintenance, originally due to finish July 6, 2026, was repeatedly interrupted: GE Vernova evacuated engineers for nine days in May 2026 amid militia clashes near the plant, and again in August 2026 after a drone attack forced an emergency evacuation; GE Vernova also acknowledged technical difficulties contributed to the delay. The restored capacity offers modest relief for western Libya's grid after a summer of prolonged blackouts that fueled nationwide civil-disobedience protests.

title: Anti-Illegal Migration Agency Transfers 50 Sudanese Migrants With Infectious Diseases From Benghazi to Al-Kufra
detail: Libya's eastern Anti-Illegal Migration Agency began transferring 50 Sudanese migrants described as having infectious diseases from the Greater Benghazi detention center to Al-Kufra on September 4, 2026, in preparation for their removal from Libyan territory. The operation, overseen by agency head Major General Salah Mahmoud Al-Khafifi and branch administration director Major General Abdelali Suleiman, was attended by representatives of the Sudanese consulate and presented as part of the agency's ongoing removal plans and crackdown on irregular migration. It follows similar recent transfers, including batches of 109 and 200 migrants moved from Benghazi to Kufra ahead of deportation.
